value: The unit bi-octonions form a Moufang loop, the Lorentz super-loop, that contains $SL(2,\mathbb C)$ and eight spinor charges; these are carried by an isodoublet of DiracLike spinors on Minkowski space (Dirac spinors of $SL(2,\mathbb C)$ that have electric charge zero and no electroweak quantum numbers, particles not yet observed), coupled to a new gauge group $SL(2,\mathbb C)\times SU(2)_{\rm v}\times U(1)^{\rm F}$ of the local Lorentz transformations, a vector-like isospin and the fermion number. With a contact self-interaction whose spin-zero pair channel is supercritical, the spinor field condenses into a superfluid whose order parameter is a composite isospin vector of fermion number two. We solve it in five mean-field methods (Hubbard-Stratonovich with three decouplings, Kohn-Sham, and Cornwall-Jackiw-Tomboulis) and derive its effective Lagrangians. In every method the condensate is the Higgs field of the new group: the isospin bosons $W^\pm$ and the fermion-number boson $Z$ become massive, and exactly one gauge boson stays massless. This boson, which we name the zeugon, is not the photon: it couples to the unbroken isospin charge, it is the only gauge boson that attracts the two members of a pair, and, because the surviving group is $SL(2,\mathbb C)\times O(2)$, its charge conjugation is itself a gauge symmetry, the structure of Alice electrodynamics. The amplitude mode is a composite scalar bound below the threshold of two quasi-particles; once it can decay into the longitudinal gauge bosons its width is $2.1\mbox{--}3.9$ times its mass. From the static pair response we compute the gradient coefficient of the order parameter at the critical temperature and find Ginzburg numbers 7.6\mbox{--}11: the critical region is wider than the critical temperature itself, and the mean-field transition is not reliable. The Higgs particle of the new group is therefore composite and broad. Because the condensate is a singlet of the electroweak group, it cannot be the Higgs boson observed at the LHC. We outline how gravitation enters through E.~A.~Lord's gauge theory of the local change of spinor representation, for which the $SL(2,\mathbb C)$ factor of the gauge group is the natural place; the gravitational sector is not computed here.
